children: appears placid on the surface, underlying individual stocks are experiencing wild volatility reminiscent of a full-blown crisis, according to Nomura strategist Charlie McElligott.

The S&P 500 moved just 0.8% over the past month, while the average constituent stock swung by 8.9%, McElligott wrote in a recent note. This 8.1 percentage point dispersion gap ranks in the 95th percentile of historical data over the past 30 years, reflecting an extraordinary level of churn beneath a deceptively quiet benchmark.

McElligott stressed that far from being complacent, the market is undergoing a substantial “rolling correction” driven by rising interest rate pressures and severe capital displacement toward artificial intelligence. Over the trailing 30 days, Technology, Media, and Telecommunication, or TMT, and Energy
were the only S&P 500 sectors to post positive returns, while rate-sensitive sectors took a heavy beating—led by real estate investment trusts

Damage across individual constituents is widespread: 85% of S&P 500 stocks were down more than 10% from their all-time highs, and 59% were in deep bear-market territory, down over 20%, the strategist noted. The benchmark's stability is almost single-handedly anchored by a tiny cluster of mega-cap AI leaders, with just ten stocks—led by Nvidia
—accounting for 70% of the market's 23% rally since late March.

title: S&P 500 flatline masks historic churn across individual stocks - Nomura
